input.quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
input.rationale: Two material failures against the fallback. (1) Section 4.1 (p0024) gives only a passive, symmetric right embedded in the auto-renewal sentence — "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — which neither states a Company convenience right nor confines HDI to the end of a term (the following sentence lets the terminating party specify any date 90+ days out). Operation 2 therefore adds the missing right as a standalone sentence, and Operation 1 rewrites the renewal limb so HDI's convenience termination is available only at the end of a term on ninety (90) days' notice to the Company, which also cures the dangling "to the other" antecedent and, by saying "for convenience", leaves HDI's for-cause rights (e.g. Section 1.6) unaffected. The two operations are complementary, not duplicative: the Company's right moves out of the passive limb into its own sentence. (2) Section 4.2(a) (p0026) imposes on the Company alone a Termination Payment of half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly instalments (p0029) with no reciprocal HDI payment (p0028) — about $600,000 on $2,000,000 of Net Sales versus roughly $140,000 of three months' Section 3.1 fees. Operation 3 adds a three-month fee ceiling as prong (ii) of a "lesser of" and keeps the original computation as prong (i), so no payment arises at or below $800,000 of trailing Net Sales and Section 4.2(b)'s netting still operates; 4.2(c), the Termination Date definition, the one-year term and the renewal structure are untouched. Preferred is not claimed (notice stays at 90 rather than 30 days; no prepaid fees exist to refund under this revenue-share model), and the breach carve-out to 4.2(a) is left to the breach/remedies rule.

proposal.summary: Add a standalone Company right to terminate for convenience at any time on 90 days' notice, confine HDI's convenience termination to the end of a term on 90 days' notice to the Company, and cap the Termination Payment at three months of Section 3.1 fees.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4.1 now carries our convenience right in its own sentence — the Company may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice — and HDI's convenience right is confined to the end of a term on the same notice to us, leaving its for-cause rights untouched. In Section 4.2(a) the Termination Payment is capped at three months of Section 3.1 fees as a ceiling on the existing calculation, so Section 4.2(b)'s netting outcome is preserved. We will raise separately that 4.2(a) should not bite where we terminate for HDI's breach.

ops.oldText: unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
ops.newText: unless terminated by HDI for convenience, only at the end of a term, upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company.

ops.text: The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI.

ops.oldText: the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: the amount of which shall be the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.
